queries: Do statins lower the risk of breast cancer recurrence?
How much vitamin D should older adults take?
Should governments ban private cars from city centres?
What causes inflation to rise quickly?
Effects of intermittent fasting on insulin sensitivity
passages: In a cohort of 18,000 women with early-stage breast cancer, statin use after diagnosis was associated with a lower rate of recurrence over ten years.
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase and are prescribed to lower LDL cholesterol in patients at risk of cardiovascular disease.
Mammography screening every two years reduced breast cancer mortality among women aged 50 to 69.
Guidelines recommend 800 to 1,000 IU of vitamin D daily for adults over 70 to reduce fracture risk.
Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin after exposure to ultraviolet B light and is also found in oily fish.
Calcium supplements taken without vitamin D showed little benefit for bone density in older women.
Banning cars from city centres cuts air pollution and makes streets safer for pedestrians and cyclists.
Car-free zones hurt small shops that depend on customers who drive in from the suburbs.
Public transport investment is a precondition for reducing car traffic in dense cities.
Inflation rises quickly when demand outpaces supply, for example after large fiscal stimulus or supply-chain shocks.
Central banks raise interest rates to cool demand and bring inflation back toward target.
Wage-price spirals occur when rising prices lead to higher wage demands, which push prices up further.
Intermittent fasting improved insulin sensitivity in overweight adults compared with daily calorie restriction.
Time-restricted eating aligns food intake with circadian rhythms and may lower fasting glucose.
Skipping breakfast was associated with higher body weight in several observational studies.
